title: Why Flamingos Are Pink Revealed | Chemistry
description: Ever wonder why flamingos are bright pink? It is not just their diet, but a specific chemical process happening inside their bodies.
instagram_caption: The secret behind the flamingo's pink feathers. Follow Wonders of the Nature for more.

segments.narration: Flamingos are born grey and look like dull little balls of fluff.
They eventually turn vibrant pink after eating a very specific diet of food.
They feast on algae and tiny shrimp filled with colorful natural plant pigments.
Your body would stay the same but a flamingo processes this pigment differently.
The bird's digestive system breaks down these carotenoid chemicals into tiny orange fats.
These fat molecules then move through the blood to reach their growing feathers.
Over time the pigment settles into the feathers creating that signature bright glow.

segments.narration: The more shrimp they eat the more intense the pink color becomes naturally.
If a flamingo stops eating these special foods its color eventually fades away.
The pink intensity is basically a status symbol showing they are healthy birds.
This wild transformation is one of nature's most brilliant and colorful chemical tricks.
